declarations.description:
A context menu of the items an app hands it, at a point of the viewport: show() opens it,
a choice sends `dex-action` and closes it, and Escape, a click or a right-click outside it,
or a scroll close it. Whichever way it closes, it sends `dex-menu-closed`. Arrow keys move
along the items, disabled ones included (their `reason` is their tooltip), and Enter chooses.
The tree table's items for a selection are buildContextMenuItems'
(`data-explorer-view/tree-table`).
declarations.name: DexContextMenu

members.name: show
members.description:
Opens the menu with these items, its top-left corner at (`x`, `y`) in viewport pixels
(a contextmenu event's clientX and clientY), moved in to fit the viewport. A menu already
open is replaced: it closes first, and says so (`dex-menu-closed`).

members.name: close
members.description: Closes the menu, choosing nothing. An open menu says so (`dex-menu-closed`).

events.name: dex-menu-closed
events.description:
The open menu closed, whichever way: after a choice (and its `dex-action`), on Escape, a
click, a right-click or a scroll outside it, on close(), or as show() replaced its items.
connectTable hears it, so that a menu several tables share forgets which one opened it. No
detail.

events.name: dex-action
events.description: An item that is not disabled was chosen, by a click or Enter; the menu closes.

declarations.name: defineContextMenu
declarations.description: Registers the widget as `<dex-context-menu>`, or under `tag`.

A modal dialog that says why something the user did was refused: a title, the reason, the
value entered beside the one kept, and a detail line. show() opens it; OK, Escape or a click
outside it closes it, and focus goes back where it was. With `showRevert`, a Revert button
sends `dex-revert` first. Tab stays inside the dialog while it is open.
declarations.name: DexErrorDialog

members.name: show
members.description:
Opens the dialog, focused on OK (never on Revert, which discards the user's edit).

`title` defaults to 'Invalid Value' and `reason` to 'The entered value is not valid.';
`invalidValue` and `validValue` are shown as Entered and Previous, `detail` under them, and
`showRevert` adds the Revert button. Focus returns to `returnFocusTo` when it closes, or to
the element that had it when this was called.

members.name: hide
members.description: Closes the dialog and gives focus back, sending nothing.

events.name: dex-revert
events.description: Revert was pressed: put back the value kept. The dialog closes. No detail.

declarations.name: defineErrorDialog
declarations.description: Registers the widget as `<dex-error-dialog>`, or under `tag`.

declarations.name: connectHierarchy
declarations.description:
Wire `element` to `hierarchy`: draw its rows now, and again on each of its refreshes and
rebuilds, and answer each row the user opens.

A folder's hierarchy as a tree: each project and folder, the files in it, and under each file
the files it references, opened a level at a time. The rows are HierarchyItems
(`data-explorer-view/model`'s FolderHierarchy makes them); the rows under one are asked of
`loadChildren` as it is first opened, and asked again when `items` is replaced. A row reads its
file's name and kind, an unresolved reference a warning, and a file's mark a badge (a circular
reference, unsaved changes).

A click or Enter chooses a row: it is selected, `dex-hierarchy-select` says which file it opens,
and a row with rows under it opens or closes. The arrow keys move through the rows (Right opens
a row or goes into it, Left closes it or goes to its parent), Home and End go to the first and
the last. `revealRow` shows a row the app names (the file it has open), and `expandTopLevel`
opens the folder's own row on first show. connectHierarchy wires one to a FolderHierarchy.
declarations.name: DexHierarchy

members.name: items
members.description: The top-level rows. Replacing them asks `loadChildren` again for every open row. Default none.

members.name: loadChildren
members.description:
What answers the rows under a row, as it is first opened: a FolderHierarchy's `children`.
Null, the default, opens every row onto nothing.

members.name: expandedKeys
members.description:
The keys of the open rows. The tree changes it as the user opens and closes rows; a row
whose key is here opens as soon as it is shown. Default none.

members.name: selectedKey
members.description: The key of the selected row, or null. The tree changes it as the user chooses; setting it sends nothing.

members.name: label
members.description: What a screen reader calls the tree. Default `Files`. Attribute `label`.

members.name: expandTopLevel
members.description:
Open each top-level row (a folder's own row, each project's) the first time the tree shows it,
by adding its key to `expandedKeys`, as a table opens its sections; after that the row stays
as the user leaves it, through new `items` too. Another folder's rows are new rows, and open.
Off, the default, a folder opens closed. Attribute `expand-top-level`.

members.name: revealRow
members.description:
Show a row: open each row of `path` but the last (the rows from a top-level row down to it,
as FolderHierarchy's `pathTo` gives them), select the last, and scroll it into view as soon as
it is drawn, once the rows above it are read. The keyboard goes on from it. It takes no focus,
and a choice of the user's before the row is drawn leaves the scroll undone.

Sends nothing, unless `options.choose`: then `dex-hierarchy-select` for the row, as a click on
it sends, without opening or closing it. connectHierarchy's `reveal(uri)` finds the path to a
file's row.

events.name: dex-hierarchy-select
events.description:
A row was chosen, by a click or Enter, and is now the selected one: the file it opens, or
null for a row that is no file. Sent again each time a row is chosen.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: What a screen reader calls the tree. Default `Files`. Attribute `label`.

attributes.name: expand-top-level
attributes.description:
Open each top-level row (a folder's own row, each project's) the first time the tree shows it,
by adding its key to `expandedKeys`, as a table opens its sections; after that the row stays
as the user leaves it, through new `items` too. Another folder's rows are new rows, and open.
Off, the default, a folder opens closed. Attribute `expand-top-level`.

cssProperties.name: --dex-selection-fg
cssProperties.description: The ink on a selected row, whose surface is --dex-color-accent-bg.

declarations.name: defineHierarchy
declarations.description: Registers the widget as `<dex-hierarchy>`, or under `tag`, and the `<dex-icon>` its rows draw.

declarations.name: useIconAssets
declarations.description:
Draws every `<dex-icon>` from the icon files the app's bundler copied, with no copy step and no
setIconBase: this module names each icon as `new URL('…/<id>.svg', import.meta.url)`, which Vite,
webpack 5 and Parcel turn into an asset of the build. Call it once, before the first icon is
drawn, as setIconBase; a setIconBase after it goes back to a folder.

Importing this entry is what puts the icons into a bundle — all of them, renamed — so an app
that ships the folder as files already (VS Code's extension does) leaves it out.

A MATLAB project's page: what it is, its startup and shutdown files, shortcuts, path, labels,
locations and the projects it references, from the message `projectPageMessage` builds. Each
section with many rows has a filter, and one past its cap a Show all; both are kept across a
new page of the same project (a store saved on disk), and dropped for another project. A link
to a file or a project is the app's to open: a click, Enter or Space sends `dex-project-open`.

The page is in the element's shadow root with its stylesheet adopted, so it needs no
`style-src 'unsafe-inline'`, and the page's class names reach nothing else on the page.
declarations.name: DexProjectPage

members.name: payload
members.description:
The project shown: `projectPageMessage`'s answer (its `type` is ignored), or null for none.
A page of another project (another `root`) starts with every filter cleared; a page of the
same one keeps them. Setting it clears `error`.

members.name: error
members.description: Why the project could not be shown, above the page; empty for nothing to say. Attribute `error`.

events.name: dex-project-open
events.description: A link to a file, a folder or a project was followed, by a click, Enter or Space.

attributes.name: error
attributes.description: Why the project could not be shown, above the page; empty for nothing to say. Attribute `error`.

declarations.name: defineProjectPage
declarations.description: Registers the widget as `<dex-project-page>`, or under `tag`.

declarations.name: FILTER_THRESHOLD
declarations.description: A filter box appears above this many items.

declarations.name: ROW_CAP
declarations.description: Rows rendered before a "Show all" button takes over.

declarations.name: esc
declarations.description:
Everything that reaches the markup, escaped — the page's single rule.

Numbers are accepted, not just strings, so a count is escaped by the same call as
the name beside it. Counts look exempt — a count is declared a number, and a number
cannot carry a `<` — but that type is a claim core's parser makes, and this
page sits on the far side of a postMessage boundary, where the payload is JSON and
nothing re-checks the declaration. While this took `string` only, a count could not
use it and was concatenated bare instead; `memberCount` then rendered escaped in the
identity block and raw in the Labels header, one field under two rules, and the
second was the wrong one (CodeQL js/xss, 2026-10-01).

`null` is NOT in the parameter type and must not be added. `memberCount` and friends are
nullable for a format that records no member list, and this signature is what turns one
of them reaching the markup into a compile error at the call site instead of the word
'null' on a customer's page — core's ProjectPage.memberCount relies on that by name.
Widening here, or defaulting the argument, moves the decision out of the renderer that
has to make it (see labelsSection).

`'` is deliberately absent: every attribute written here is double-quoted, and the
test that pins that is the reminder to keep it so.

declarations.name: filterTerms
declarations.description:
Split a filter query into terms.

Bare terms only: whitespace-separated, case-insensitive substring, ANDed. This is
deliberately NOT the table's `rowFilter.ts` grammar, which is column-aware
(`Name:foo`, comparison operators) and needs each row to be a record of named
columns. A page section is not a table — Project Path rows have one field, Labels
are chips and are not filtered at all — so adopting that grammar would mean
inventing column names per section to expose a syntax nobody asked for. What IS
shared is the part a user actually types: several words, all of which must appear.

declarations.name: highlight
declarations.description:
Escaped `text` with every occurrence of every term wrapped in `<mark>`.

Overlapping and adjacent hits are merged before wrapping. Two terms that overlap
in one word (`sup` and `upp` in "support") would otherwise emit nested or
interleaved marks, i.e. broken markup, from input the user typed by accident.

declarations.name: renderProjectPage
declarations.description: The whole page.

declarations.description: Tells every `` where the icon files are: the URL of a folder holding the files of this package's `icons/` (`data-explorer-view/icons/*`), to which `.svg` is appended. A relative URL resolves as any `` does, against the page's base URL. The default is the package's own folder, found from this module's URL. That holds wherever the package's files are served as they are installed — a static server, an import map, a dev server that does not bundle dependencies. A bundler moves this module into a chunk of its own, from which that path leads nowhere: an app that bundles copies the icons to where it serves its assets and calls this with that folder, before the first icon renders, since nothing redraws the icons already on the page.

declarations.name: hiddenStyles
declarations.description:
The `hidden` attribute, honoured.

The browser hides `[hidden]` with a user-agent rule, and every widget's own `:host` rule sets
`display`, which beats it: `table.hidden = true` used to leave the table on screen. Important,
so it also beats a page rule that gives the element a display of its own — hidden means hidden,

Forced-colors / high-contrast mode styles.
Ensures all interactive elements have visible borders and focus indicators

declarations.name: hasLineBreak
declarations.description: Whether `text` holds a line break of any kind (LF, CRLF or a lone CR).

declarations.name: withHeldLineBreaks
declarations.description:
What to post for `typed`, read back from a textarea seeded with `held`. `held` itself where the
two differ only in how their line breaks are spelled: nothing was edited, so the caller posts
nothing. Otherwise `typed` with each line break spelled as `held` spelled it, matched by the
lines around it rather than by its place in the list, so that a line added or removed in a text
mixing two kinds leaves every other break as it was: the lines `typed` begins with as `held`
does keep the breaks after them, and the lines it ends with as `held` does keep the breaks
before them. A break between edited lines is spelled as most of `held`'s are (the first such
kind, on a tie), and as LF, MATLAB's `newline`, where `held` has none.

declarations.name: connectTable
declarations.description:
Wire `table` to `source`: show what it answers, and answer what the table asks. Returns the
handle that says what the app is to do (`on`), and through which it selects.

The table is left to the app in what it is (`readonly`, `canAdd`, `rowDrag`, `storageKey`):
connectTable sets `loading` until the first paint, `expandTopLevel`, and what each paint says.

The `+ Add` gallery: a popover of tiles, one per kind of entry a dictionary's sections take
(or per class a MAT-file takes), grouped by section. A click on a tile sends `dex-add-tile`;
the table turns it into `dex-add-entry`. Its Keep open box pins it open across adds
(`dex-add-pin-changed`), and Escape asks to close it (`dex-add-closed`). The tiles are one tab
stop, and the arrow keys move between them. `<dex-tree-table>` draws it, under its search bar.
declarations.name: DexAddGallery

members.name: pinned
members.description:

session: a user who pins is telling you about their next several minutes, not about

dictionary's gallery. Given, the tiles are those classes' (the model's matCatalog): a MAT-file has

Default null. Property only.

events.name: dex-add-pin-changed

events.name: dex-add-closed

The tree table's search bar: the applied filter as one chip per condition, and an input for
what the user is still typing. It filters nothing and keeps no filter: each gesture — Enter on
the input, a chip's ×, the clear button, a second Escape — proposes a replacement for the whole
text in `dex-filter-applied`, and the table applies it and sets `text` and `tokens` back.
`<dex-tree-table>` draws it.
declarations.name: DexFilterBar

members.name: text
members.description:
The applied filter text. The bar never mutates it; it proposes replacements. Default ''.
Attribute `text`.

members.name: tokens
members.description:
Its parse, from the table's one `parseFilterExpression` call: one chip each. Default none.
Property only.

members.name: placeholder
members.description: The input's placeholder. Default 'Search'. Attribute `placeholder`.

members.name: focusInput
members.description: Focuses (and selects) the input — the Ctrl+F entry point, forwarded by the table's focusFilter.

events.name: dex-filter-applied
events.description:
The user asked for this filter text: Enter on what they typed (added after the applied
text), a chip removed, or the whole filter cleared. The table handles it and lets it on.

attributes.description:
The applied filter text. The bar never mutates it; it proposes replacements. Default ''.
Attribute `text`.

attributes.name: placeholder

declarations.name: defineFilterBar
declarations.description: Registers the widget as `<dex-filter-bar>`, or under `tag`.

The tree table: a document's rows as a tree, with a search bar, sortable, resizable and
reorderable columns (the Columns menu shows, hides and orders them, and a right-click on a
header filters on that column), cell editors, row drag and drop, links, matrix glyphs, an
`+ Add` gallery and virtual scrolling for very large documents. Data comes in by properties
(`rows` above all) and every user action goes out as a `dex-*` event; it never changes the
document itself. Its defaults are a full editor; `readonly`, `canAdd` and `rowDrag` turn parts
of that off.
declarations.name: DexTreeTable

members.name: rows
members.description:
The rows, flat: each names its parent by `ID` (`parent`, null at the top level), and
siblings show in the order given until the user sorts. What the model's planner makes of a
document, `rowPlannerFor(name).payload(node, LAZY_ROW_BUDGET).rows`, which holds back the
children of rows past the budget (`_lazy`) for `dex-request-children` to fetch. Default none.
Attribute `rows` (JSON); set the property.

members.name: selectedRowIds
members.description:
The ids of the selected rows. The table changes it as the user selects, and says so with
`dex-row-selected`; setting it sends nothing. Default none. Attribute `selectedrowids` (JSON).

members.name: rowHeight
members.description:
The row height virtual scrolling lays rows out at, in CSS pixels, when the page sets no
`--dex-row-height`; with the token set, the token's. Rows are drawn at the token, or 28px
without one, so to change the height set the token, which both read. Default 28. Attribute
`rowheight`.

members.name: tableStyle
members.description:
`normal`, the default, rules every cell; `light` drops the lines between columns and keeps a
faint one between rows. Reflected to the attribute `table-style`.

members.name: columnLabels
members.description:
Each column's header text, by column key (`{ DataType: 'Data Type' }`), also the name a
search may qualify a term with (`"Data Type":double`); a column with none shows its key.
Default null. Attribute `columnlabels` (JSON).

members.name: columnGroups
members.description:
The group heading each column sits under in the Columns menu, by column key. Default null:
no headings. Attribute `columngroups` (JSON).

members.name: columns
members.description:
The column keys this document has, which the Columns menu offers; the user's saved order and
choice of hidden ones apply within them. Default null: the built-in set. Attribute `columns`
(JSON).

members.name: banners
members.description:
The banners drawn above the search bar: an error, a notice, and what the document's read
could not read (TableBanners), each when present. connectTable sets it from what its source
says. Default null: none. Property only.

members.name: loading
members.description:
The rows are on their way: while there are none, the table says Loading… (with a spinner,
after half a second) instead of "No data"; the search bar stays. Set it while a document is
read. Default false. Attribute `loading`.

members.name: canAdd
members.description:
Whether this view can create entries, i.e. whether the `+ Add` button (and its gallery,
whose tiles send `dex-add-entry`) exists at all. Default false. Attribute `canadd`.

members.name: addClasses
members.description:
The classes a MAT-file's gallery offers, as core lists the classes a MAT-file can hold, or
null, the default, for a dictionary's gallery, which offers every tile. The gallery draws the
tiles of these classes only (the model's matCatalog). Property only.

members.name: rowDrag
members.description:
Whether a row can be dragged, or a dragged row let go over one. Set it false where the
document cannot be changed: no row is draggable, and a drag from another table draws no drop
target here, on a row or on the empty body. Default true. Attribute `rowdrag`.

members.name: readonly
members.description:
A viewer: the user selects, opens, searches, sorts, filters and copies, and changes nothing.
No cell editor opens — not on a double-click, not on Enter, not for beginRename or
openWholeValueEditor — and no cell is drawn as editable; the `+ Add` button is not drawn
whatever canAdd says, and no row is dragged or takes a drop whatever rowDrag says. So none of
the events those gestures send (dex-edit-completed, dex-edit-text-request, dex-add-entry,
dex-row-drag-start, dex-row-drop) is sent. A right-click still sends dex-table-context-menu:
what a read-only menu offers is the app's to say (buildContextMenuItems with editable false).
False, the default, is the table as it always was, each cell's own flags deciding. Reflected
to the attribute `readonly`.

members.name: storageKey
members.description:
Where the user's column choices (which are shown, and their order) are kept: the page's
localStorage, under `<storageKey>-column-order`, `<storageKey>-hidden-columns` and
`<storageKey>-known-columns`. The default, 'dex', is the keys every table has always used,
so a layout saved before this existed carries over — and every table on the page that keeps
the default shares one layout. An app gives each kind of table a key of its own, or null
(or '') to keep the choices for this element's life only, with localStorage never touched.
They are read when the table is connected, so set it before the table goes into the page: a
key set later reads them again, from that key, after the table has shown the ones under the
key it had. Attribute `storage-key`.

members.name: selectedRowId
members.description:
The last of `selectedRowIds`, or '' when nothing is selected; set, it selects that row alone
('' selects nothing). Sends nothing.

members.name: expandedIds
members.description:
The rows shown open, by id: a copy, the caller's to keep.

Set it to open exactly these rows — an expansion the app saved, or the one it read before
giving the table new rows (nextExpandedIds keeps those that still exist). An id with no row is
kept, and opens its row if one comes. Setting it fetches nothing; expand() is the twisty's
click, which asks for children the payload held back.

members.name: expand
members.description:
Opens these rows as a click on each one's twisty does: a row with nothing under it stays
closed, and a row whose children the payload held back (`_lazy`) asks for them once
(dex-request-children). Read off `rows` as they are now, so it may follow an assignment of
them directly.

members.name: collapse
members.description: Closes these rows.

members.name: expandTopLevel
members.description:
The expansion an app otherwise keeps around every assignment of `rows`, kept by the table
(nextExpandedIds): the first rows with any in them open their top level — a dictionary's
sections, a MAT-file's variables, though not one whose children were held back, whose first
click fetches — and from then on the rows the user opened stay open while they exist, and
what they closed stays closed. Off, the default, a change of `rows` leaves the expansion as it
was, to the app (expandedIds). Attribute `expand-top-level`.

members.name: dropPredictor

type.text:
| ((
        targetRowId: string,
        mode: 'copy' | 'move',
      ) => { canDrop: boolean; cursor: string; tooltip: string; noop: boolean } | null)
    | null

members.description:
Predicts a drop for the row under the cursor ('' for the space under the rows), as the
dragover goes: whether it may drop, the cursor and the tooltip to show, and whether it would
change nothing. The app sets it, from the model's dropDecision and what it knows is being
dragged (a drag can come from another table). Returns null when it cannot predict — no drag
it was told about, or a target with no rule — and null REFUSES: with a predictor, "cannot
say" is not "yes". With none, the default, any row takes a drop and the space under the rows
takes none. Property only.

members.name: toggleAddGallery
members.description:
Opens the `+ Add` gallery under the Add button, or closes it if it is open, as a click on the
button does: an app's keyboard shortcut for adding an entry. It opens nothing while the button
is not drawn (`canAdd` false, or `readonly`).

members.name: beginRename
members.description:
Opens the Name editor on a row, as a double-click on its Name does: what an app calls after
adding an entry the user should name (`dex-add-entry`'s `rename`). The edit comes back as
`dex-edit-completed`. Returns whether the editor opened: false when the row is not in `rows`
yet, so an app can call again once it is, or when its Name cannot be edited.

members.name: openWholeValueEditor
members.description:
The answer to `dex-edit-text-request`: opens the Value editor of `rowId` on `text`, the whole
value the cell's summary stands for. In a textarea, as the text can be one long line of up to
200,000 characters; committed unchanged it sends nothing, and changed it sends
`dex-edit-completed` with the whole text. Only the answer to the last request opens an
editor, and only while no other editor is open and the cell still takes this one: an answer
that arrives after the user moved on opens nothing.

members.name: focusFilter
members.description: Focuses (and selects) the search input: an app's Ctrl+F.

members.name: flashRow
members.description: Flashes a row's background once, on the next render, as a copy does; nothing if it is not drawn.

events.name: dex-add-entry
events.description: A tile of the `+ Add` gallery was clicked: add one entry of that class, renaming it if `rename`.

events.name: dex-request-children
events.description:
A row whose children the payload held back (`_lazy`) was opened: answer with its rows,
merged into `rows` under it (the model's childRowsMessage builds them with the file's
planner, and mergeChildRows puts them in place). Asked once until its rows arrive.

events.name: dex-table-context-menu
events.description:
A right-click on a row (after selecting it) or on the space under the rows: open a context
menu there.

events.name: dex-row-selected
events.description:
The user changed the selection: a click, Ctrl/Cmd- or Shift-click, a key, select-all, or a
right-click on a row not in it.

events.name: dex-row-drag-start
events.description: The user started dragging rows.

events.name: dex-row-drag-end
events.description: A drag of this table's rows ended, dropped or not. No detail.

events.name: dex-row-drop
events.description:
Rows were let go over a row the dropPredictor accepts (any row, with no predictor), or over
the space under the rows when it accepts that.

events.name: dex-edit-text-request
events.description: A Value editor is opening on a summary: send the whole text with openWholeValueEditor.

events.name: dex-edit-completed
events.description: A cell edit was committed with a text that differs from the one it had.

events.name: dex-link-clicked
events.description:
A link in a cell was clicked: a Data Type, Used By, a block or a parameter. `target` says
what it points at; see LinkClickedDetail for its forms.

declarations.name: defineTreeTable
declarations.description:
Registers the widget as `<dex-tree-table>`, or under `tag`, after the parts its template draws,
which keep their default names: the + Add gallery, the column-filter popup, the filter bar, the
icon and the matrix glyph. Parts first, so a part whose name is taken throws before the table
is registered at all.

declarations.name: shouldShowContextMenu
declarations.description:
Whether a right-click should open the context menu at all. Read-only
documents get NO menu — the read-only byte-backed view has no copy/paste/
mutation handlers, so an all-disabled menu would be dead UI.

declarations.name: shouldOpenCellEditor
declarations.description:
Whether a double-click / Enter should open the inline cell editor. Gated on
the document-level flag only: read-only documents never open the editor,
regardless of any per-row `editable` flag (which is a coloring signal).

declarations.name: buildContextMenuItems
declarations.description:
Build the right-click context menu for the CURRENT SELECTION.

Pure and synchronous: enablement comes from the host-computed row flags, the cached
clipboard state, the target section's rules, and whether the document is editable —
no round-trip. Two things it deliberately does NOT decide: which rows are operands
(resolveOperands does, so the keyboard cannot diverge) and whether a payload may land
in a section (dropDecision.rejectReason does, so a Paste offered here is a drop the
hover feedback would allow).

GROUPS, THEN JOIN. The items are built as groups and the separators are put between
whatever groups survive. A section header's menu — Paste, then Undo/Redo — then falls
out of dropping the two empty groups, with no case of its own; so does the binary
format's missing "Location in Text". Managing separators by hand is how a menu ends
up with two in a row or one at the bottom, and that is exactly what this shape makes
impossible.

A matrix's cells as a read-only grid, one page at a time, headed by MATLAB's 1-based row and
column numbers, with a page selector over the dimensions past the second. Only the cells near
the scroll position are built, so a 1000x1000 page scrolls as a small one does. The arrow
keys, Home and End move between cells and PageUp and PageDown between pages; a cell whose text
is clipped shows it whole as its tooltip. Escape is left to the panel around it.
`<dex-variable-editor>` draws it.
declarations.name: DexMatrixGrid

members.name: matrix
members.description: The matrix shown, cells included; null, the default, draws nothing. Property only.

members.name: pageCount
members.description: How many pages the matrix has: the product of its dimensions past the second, 1 for 2-D.

members.name: page
members.description: The page shown, from 0; set, it is clamped to the pages there are.

members.name: pageLabel
members.description: A page's subscript as MATLAB writes it, `(:,:,2)` or `(:,:,1,3)`; '' for a 2-D matrix.

members.name: cellText
members.description: The text of cell (`r`, `c`), from 0, of a page (the one shown by default); '' outside the matrix.

members.name: focusActiveCell
members.description: Focuses the cell the keyboard is on, (1,1) until it has moved.

declarations.name: defineMatrixGrid
declarations.description: Registers the widget as `<dex-matrix-grid>`, or under `tag`.

The variable editor: a panel, anchored under the glyph that opened it, that shows a matrix's
cells in a `<dex-matrix-grid>`. An app makes one and appends it to the page; show() opens it
on a matrix's descriptor, with its title and a waiting line, and deliver() fills it in with
the cells once the app has them. Escape, the close button, a click outside it or a scroll
close it, and focus goes back to the glyph if the panel held it. It sends no events.
declarations.name: DexVariableEditor

members.name: show
members.description:
Opens the panel under `anchorEl` (the glyph, which gets focus back) on what the row knew:
name, class, shape, node id. The cells are not here yet — the app fetches them for
`matrix.nodeId` (the model's matrixCellsMessage builds the answer) and hands it to
deliver(). Until then the panel shows its title and a waiting line.

members.name: deliver
members.description:
The cells the app fetched for the panel show() opened: fills the panel in, or says why it
cannot be filled in (the answer's `message`). Ignores an answer that is not about what is
currently on screen: open A, change your mind, open B, and A's reply can still be in flight —
taking it would put A's numbers under B's title, which is worse than a slow panel.

members.name: close
members.description: Closes the panel; focus goes back to the glyph that opened it, if the panel held it.

members.name: reposition
members.description:
Places the panel again under its glyph, left edges aligned, pulled in at the viewport's
edges and flipped above the glyph when there is no room below. show() and deliver() call it.

declarations.name: defineVariableEditor
declarations.description: Registers the widget as `<dex-variable-editor>`, or under `tag`, after the grid it shows.
